title: Predictive headroom projection and tiered memory budgeting for mixed weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need a predictive headroom projection module and an accompanying tiered memory-budgeting policy that dynamically apportions GPU memory across model weights, KV cache, and activations for mixed-priority inference workloads. The goal is to reduce OOMs and tail-latency spikes while preserving throughput and lowering token cost via better continuous batching and preemptive eviction signals.

Problem details: Current heuristics allocate fixed soft quotas for weights/KV/activations and rely on reactive eviction once pressure is high. This causes: increased OOM risk for sudden long-context requests, inefficient conservative limits for multi-tenant bursts, and missed opportunities to opportunistically batch when predicted headroom is sufficient.

Proposed approach: 1) Build a lightweight predictive headroom estimator (PHE) that consumes streaming telemetry: per-tenant 95th/median seq-length, request arrival rates, active model variants + weight residency sizes, KV occupancy histogram and decay half-life under current workload. 2) Use a probabilistic projection (quantile forecasting) to compute projected memory envelope for the next 60s/5min windows and recommend an "elastic headroom" buffer sized to target an acceptable tail OOM probability (configurable, default 0.1%). 3) Implement a tiered budgeting policy: "core weights" (pinned resident weights), "preferred KV" (hot KV slots retained based on recency and priority), "ephemeral activations" (spillable to host or compressed). The policy exposes a graded eviction cascade and preemption signals to the continuous-batcher. 4) Integrate with the runtime advisor to allow short-term optimistic batching decisions when projected headroom exceeds a safety margin. 5) Provide runtime knobs and telemetry: quantile target, projection horizon, conservative multiplier, model-priority maps.

Design constraints and trade-offs: - Keep PHE op-cost low: must run in <1ms per GPU per projection window and avoid adding heavy centralized coordination. - Conservative defaults for enterprise tenants (lower quantile target). - Prefer amortized compression over sync host spill for latency-sensitive requests. - Avoid tight coupling with scheduling; surface decision as advisory policy with automatic fallback to reactive eviction if predictions are stale.

Deliverables: - PHE module integrated into kube-agent runtime exporter and serving process. - Tiered budgeting controller with RS-eviction priorities and KV decayer. - Runtime advisor hook for continuous-batcher to consult projections. - Dashboard panels showing projection, margin, and forecast accuracy.

Long-term: Evaluate ML-based forecasting (lightweight LSTM or quantile-forecaster) if the simple exponential-decay + Poisson arrival model shows >15% error on tail projections.
acceptance_criteria: PHE computes headroom projections every 5s and writes into telemetry with latency <1ms per GPU
Tiered budgeting enforces soft reservations and triggers eviction cascade; no new OOMs in synthetic spike tests that matched historical peaks
Continuous-batcher uses advisor recommendations to increase batching size when projected headroom > margin and shows >=5% throughput improvement in controlled workload
Dashboard shows projection vs actual with mean absolute error <15% for 60s horizon on test traces
Feature gated and rolloutable by customer tier; conservative defaults applied for enterprise tenants
steps: Design: finalize PHE inputs, projection horizon defaults, and eviction tiers (3 days)
Implement: PHE library in runtime (Go) + telemetry export (5 days)
Policy: implement tiered budgeting controller and KV decayer in serving runtime (6 days)
Batcher integration: advisor hook and safety checks (3 days)
Integration tests: synthetic spike and mixed-priority scenarios (4 days)
Dashboard: minimal visualization and accuracy metrics (2 days)
Rollout: feature flag, canary on internal staging, gradual customer rollout (2 weeks)
testing_plan: Unit tests for projection math, boundary conditions, and failure modes
End-to-end local runner: replay production traces from 2026-02 to verify projections and eviction behavior
Chaos test: ramp of long-sequence requests from multiple tenants to validate no increased OOMs compared to baseline
Benchmark: throughput/latency comparison for continuous-batcher with/without advisor under identical trace
A/B on sandbox hosts for 2 weeks to measure projection accuracy and customer-visible latency impact
rollout_plan: Feature gated: default off for existing customers; opt-in by admin in Console
Canary: enable on internal infra quant-1 and a handful of non-critical customers
Monitor: 24/7 alerting on projection error >30% or OOM regression
Gradual ramp: increase percentage over 10 days, pause on signals, rollback if SLO regressions exceed threshold
Postmortem: collect a 2-week data set and decide on ML model upgrade if MAE >15%
metrics: OOM count (per-cluster) — target: decrease by >=50% on tested spike windows
Tail latency P99 for short and long requests — target: no regression >5%
Batcher throughput (tokens/sec) — target: +5% uplift under mixed load
False positive eviction rate for preferred KV — target: <2%
